full_judgment: 16. Coming to the point of limitation, which at the outset must be said is a matter of determination of fact on the evidence on record. The trial court held that the application of the co-applicant Oli Mia was barred by limitation. The trial court in its judgment has briefly referred to the evidence of P.Ws. 4 and 5 and came to a finding that Oli Mia was aware of the transfer of the case land since the inception of the proceeding. As against this the lower appellate court has very elaborately discussed this evidence on record on the point of limitation. The case of co-applicant Oli Mia was that he had no knowledge of the transfer. He came to know of the transfer in question for the first time on 20.10.73 on receipt of 'the notice of the proceeding. This assertion of the opposite party No. 1 in his pleading and in his testimony before the court was corroborated by O.P.W. 3 Radha Gobinda who admitted in his cross-examination that 011 Mia, opposite party No. I went to him with the notice and he came to know thereby that Oli Mia was unaware of the transaction before. The case of opposite party No. 1 was that he came to know for the first time on 20.10.73 on the basis of the notice Ext. B and on the contrary the pre-emptor asserted that opposite-party No. 1 knew about the transfer from before. The lower appellate court elaborately discussed the evidence of P.Ws. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 in its judgment and came to a finding that opposite party No. 1 successfully discharged his onus of proof that he came to know of the transfer in question on 20-10-73 on receipt of the notice Ext. B. On the contrary the case of the pre-emptor was that the opposite party No. 1 had know-ledge of the transfer from the very inception of the transfer but the preemption totally failed to prove this assertion of the pre-emptor by adducing any reliable witness. I have carefully gone through the judgment of the lower appellate court and the trial court on the question of limitation and I found that the lower appellate court has considered the question of limitation in pro-per perspective and after due consideration the lower appellate court disbelieved the case of the pre-emptor and accepted the case of the co-applicant Oli Mia. Mr. T. H. Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has made a grievance that the lower appellate court failed to consider the provision of sub-section (4) with regard to limitation in its proper perspective. A reference to sub-section (4) shows that any applicant or applicants may within the period referred to in sub-section (I) or within 2 months of the date of service of notice of the application under clause (b) of sub-section (3) whichever be earlier, may apply to joint in the said application. Here in the instant case the opposite party No. 1 has been able to prove by adducing oral and. documentary evidence that he came to know of the proceeding from the notice Ext. B on 20-10-73 and the application under sub-section (4) of section 96 was filed on 19-12-73 and there being no evidence on record that prior to that the co-applicant had knowledge of the transfer as contemplated in sub-section (I), the application is maintainable and the same is not barred , by limitation. Further in revisional application this court exercise a very limited jurisdiction on the question a finding of fact whether concurrent or reversal.
